paragraphs.text: Good afternoon, sisters and elders. Thanks for your letters. I'm loved reading them yesterday and today. They always uplift me. There are still a couple of you, though, who have not written me and you know who you are, so get her done.

Okay, now there's just one update. The government has decided to extend the quarantine to April 30th. We don't know all the details about that yet. It might be a little more loose, which we hope it is, but for now let's just stick with our plan and as details come out, I'll share them with you.

All right, now in your letters, I heard many of you talk about how difficult it is to sometimes keep your mind on the work and off of things that are not really that productive or uplifting. This is a problem we all face and we're going to face it pretty much all the rest of our lives. The reason is, as I've told you before, that a big purpose of our mortal probation is to learn how to control our minds and to bring them into subjection to the will of God.

Agency is the great eternal principle that, if used correctly, will bring us back in to the presence of God and allow us to become like him. Agency is the only thing we really own. God really did give it to us. Everything else we have is a stewardship from God, but when we exercise our agency correctly, we put ourselves into harmony with God's will and that pleases him.

Exercising our agency correctly also blesses us beyond our mortal understanding for sure because God loves us with a perfect love. There is simply nothing that he asks us to do that will not benefit us in wonderful ways both here and now as well as in the eternities. But with the world pressing in upon us, it is often very hard to make the right choice, especially when we are tired or fearful or feeling sorry for ourselves.

So we have to have a plan and a process firmly in our minds that we are committed to following if we're going to consistently exercise our agency correctly. The process that I've found that works best for me is the five-step process. I learned this from one of my mentors many years ago. If you have been in the mission for over a year, you have heard me talk about this before. I'm going to take the next five days of audio messages to share this process with you one step at a time so that you can understand it really well and use it to manage your agency better in the days, weeks, months and years ahead.

The first key thing to understand is that we learn by doing, not by hearing or seeing. Those senses can help us, but unless we actually do a thing, we won't really learn it. So listening to me is only a starting point for you. You must take action.

The next key thing to understand is that when we are focused on something, we have actually decided as good for us, it becomes easier to avoid things that we know are harmful to us. What this means is that we need to always have a really big goal that is important to us. Big goals that are important to us are very powerful magnets and they can keep us on the right path and away from those dead-end paths that lead us literally to disaster.

But big goals that are actually very important to us are not easy to figure out and certainly not easy to decide upon. This takes hard work, the hardest work of all really, which is thinking. Clear and constructive thinking is the hardest work in the world, which is why so few people actually do it. Most people let other people do their thinking for them and this is dangerous for a couple of reasons.

One, you might be taking your thinking from someone who isn't thinking very clearly or who doesn't really care about what's best for you. Second, when you don't do your own thinking, you never develop the brain muscles necessary to examine problems carefully and wisely. In other words, even though you have a grown-up body in your mind, you've stayed a child.

So big goals that are important to you are essential to you being able to avoid wasting your time and energy on unproductive and inappropriate thoughts and actions. Step one in this process is to set big and important goals and to always have at least one that you're working on right now. Now tomorrow we'll be talking about step two and on Thursday we'll talk about step three. Friday will be about step four. Saturday will be focused on the final step, step five. But today let's dig into step one a little more.

So in order to establish big and important goals, there are a few steps in that process. Number one, prioritize. You can have pretty much anything you want but you can't have everything you want. Life is like a giant buffet with more masarap choices than you can ever hope to eat. Choosing a goal often means rejecting some things you want in order to get other things that you want more or need more. Some people fail at this point before they've even gotten started because they're afraid to reject one alternative for a better one. They try to pursue really too many goals at once and that results in them achieving very few or probably none of them. There's an old saying that if you chase two rabbits you're going to lose them both. Don't get discouraged and don't let yourself be paralyzed by all the choices. Make your choice and get on with it. Just get started and focus on it.

Step two, think about what you want out of life and make your goals a pathway to getting it. The quality of your life ultimately depends on the quality of your decisions. You need to make sure that how you use your time is aligned with your long-term goals. What's important to you? What is not really that important to you? You need to visualize closely what your life will be like on each path and how each path fits with what you really want and enjoy. As you do this you'll literally be able to gather power not just from your own vision but from feedback from people who know you and have already succeeded in the path that you are choosing to follow.

Three, don't confuse goals with desires. A proper goal is something that you really need to achieve. Desires are just things that you want. That would be nice if you had that. But if you get distracted by desires it can prevent you from reaching your goals. Typically desires are sort of first order consequences. For example you might have a goal of physical fitness but your desire is to eat that good tasting but unhealthy food. Don't get me wrong, if you want to be a couch potato, if you want to be somebody who's just like you know just later on does nothing and doesn't have any functional health, I mean that's your choice. You can pursue whatever goals you want. But if you don't want to be out of shape and unhealthy you better get started exercising and you better not eat too much unhealthy food.

Four, don't mistake the trappings of success for success itself. Don't get into that fake it tell you make it mindset. It's a loser's mindset and smart people can spot people who have that mindset a mile away. Looking the part is important for sure but people who obsess over a $1,200 pair of shoes or a Ferrari are very rarely happy people because they don't really know what they want and they don't really know what will satisfy them and they get fooled by the false idea that there are shortcuts to your important goals. Yes there are great strategies but there are no shortcuts.

Five, never rule out a goal because you think it's unattainable. Be audacious. That's a great English word by the way, audacious. That's almost as good as masarap. Be audacious means it means be bold, be aggressive, be assertive, look for big stuff and go for the big things. There's always a best possible path. Your job is to find it for you and have the courage to follow it. What you think is attainable right now is just a function of what you know right now but once you start working on your big important goal you'll start learning a lot of things especially if you invest time with other people who also have big important goals to them. When you're with those kind of people when you're engaged in the pursuit of your goal you'll literally find paths that you never saw before. You'll learn things that you never knew before. You will learn stuff about yourself you didn't know you had.

Of course there are some impossibilities. I mean let's be honest I'm never going to play center for the Los Angeles Lakers. I never would have been able to because I'm not seven foot tall or six ten or whatever and at my age of 64 I probably can't run a four minute mile. I'm guessing no matter how hard I train. There are certainly some things like that but always remember that great expectations create great capabilities and so if you limit your goals to what you know you can achieve you're setting your goals way too low.

Six almost nothing can stop you from succeeding if you have a, flexibility and b, self-accountability. Flexibility is what allows you to accept what reality or knowledgeable people teaches you. Self-accountability is essential because if you really believe that failing to achieve a goal is your personal failure you will see your failing to achieve it as indicative that you haven't been creative enough or flexible enough or determined enough to do what it takes and you'll be that much more motivated to find the way. So don't let yourself out easy. I mean literally you got to be flexible but you're also going to be countable so don't make an excuse to let you off the hook from achieving your goal.

Seven know how to deal with setbacks. This is important. It's as important as knowing how to go forward. You're going to have setbacks. There's going to be times when you're going to just hit a roll block. There's no way to avoid it. Life's going to throw challenges at you some of which are going to be devastating challenges or at least they're going to look devastating at the time. In those bad times you might want to have your goal be just to basically hang in there to not give up to not quit to keep putting one step in front of the other. I mean I've been in those seasons in my life where my goal was literally just to get up and get dressed and go into the office. That was it because everything else just was impossible. If your mission is to always make the best possible choice and to go for it even if it's very small in some seasons of your life you will be rewarded because you will be making progress.

So elders and sisters there you have it. I hope you fully see why big goals are important and necessary for you to be able to get on the right path and stay on the right path and to really begin to see your potential. Tomorrow I will share with you some thoughts on step two which is identify and don't tolerate problems that stand in the way of you achieving those big goals you've set for yourself. Too often people are so willing to just put up with a problem. So willing does that's just the way it is. No that is not just the way it is. You don't have to tolerate problems but the first thing you have to do is identify them. We'll talk about this and how you do it tomorrow. For now we love you. Stay strong, stay calm and choose to be positive.
